The writer effectively uses sensory details to make the environment feel tangible and real. There are strong appeals to the sense of smell, such as the house smelling of "cold smoke and floor wax" and the vivid description of the fresh coffee ("dark, slightly bitter, with a hint of orange"). Sight is engaged through details like the "dried-up geranium," the "gray light of a November afternoon" pooling on the tiles, the "dark green" coat with the "worn collar," and the "gray with dust" rim of the tin. Sound and touch are also incorporated, from the memory of the warmth filling the kitchen to the careful placement of the lid to avoid making a noise, culminating in the sharp sound of a door slamming in the courtyard.
